doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Why Trump was elected, and George Will's insults
summary: She wonders how Trump was elected, with a talk of friends in England, and Rowe mentions George Will's column.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: course I’m going to — with the leadership and the government and why Donald Trump even got elected. I mean I was just Zooming with my friend in England before our talk. And they think the United States has gone berserk, like crazy, like how did you elect a person like that. And I think it’s because some people in my family, who will remain nameless, “Oh well we just wanted something different.” And I said, “But, what?” I mean I get that but that you would vote for a thing like Donald Trump who clearly has no empathy, no intellect, no experience, no understanding. It’s just so insane that people are brainwashed by reality TV or his TV show. I don’t know what it is.

I don’t either, and I’ve run out of adjectives. If you need some adjectives about him, read George Will’s latest thing for the Washington Post. He came up with some good ones. Good — you know bad good ones.

Yeah. What was that one that’s a — was it like a cockwambler or something? It was one funny real long word that was like a blustering fool who doesn’t know anything, some word that was like oh there’s Trump again. You’ve got to take out some old Victorian words or something. But I will, I’ll check that out.
